duration.text: The Architecture at Hangzhou City University is a 5 Years long program for international students, taught in English.

fees.text: Application Fee: $ 150 USD Service Fee: $ 50 USD Tuition fee: $ 2500 USD/per year ￥ 18000 CNY/per year

materials.text: 1. Non-criminal record certificate issued by the local police force.2. A letter of financial support or bank statements of the last six months from parents (including guardians).3. Application form, passport, transcripts, high school graduation certificate or notarized documents (those who have not graduated at the time of application can provide pre-graduation certificate).4. TOEFL IBT or lELTS Score Report (if available) (for English-taught program applicants whose native languageis not English) 5. Physical examination form for foreigners (medical examination results valid for 6 months)6. A passport-size electronic photo taken in the past three months. 7. Other documents that may be required by HZCU to make corrections or submit.

requirements.text: 1. Foreign citizens holding valid foreign passports, friendly to China, and with no criminal records.2. The eligibility for application should comply with the relevant regulations of China's Ministry of Education.3. Applicants should be between 18 and 25 years old and have graduated from high school.Language RequirementsFor applications to English-taught programs, the applicants must meet one of the following conditions:1. English is the native language or official language;2. Obtain a TOEFL iBT score of 78 or above, IELTS (Academic) 6.0 or above,100 or above in Duolingo, or an equivalent score in other internationally recognized English proficiency tests;3. Have obtained an academic certificate in a country where English is the native language;4. If unable to provide standardized English test scores, applicants must take the English test organized by the university.For applications to Chinese-taught programs, the applicants must have an HSK4 score of 180 or above. Applicants whose previous qualification was taught in Chinese or whose native language is Chinese may be exempt from submitting HSK scores subject to the recognition of the university.
